text:
Recent work distinguishes complementary usefulness from similarity: [ECCR (2024)](https://genai-personalization.github.io/assets/papers/GenAIRecP2024/Li.pdf) evaluates complement coherence through compatibility and relevance; [complementary reranking research (2025)](https://genai-personalization.github.io/assets/papers/GenAIRecP2025/5_Xu.pdf) likewise separates items used together from substitutes. These support an audit framework, rather than an established universal error taxonomy: immediate relevance supported by explicit feedback; broad relatedness without demonstrated current need; plausible complement; explicit compatibility conflict grounded in title/description specifications; possible redundancy; insufficient evidence. Historical interaction alone establishes neither ownership nor satisfaction. Similar items are not necessarily redundant, and missing compatibility information is not a conflict.

For the twenty-user panel, retain evidence excerpts, timestamps, feedback provenance, and confidence for each judgment. Report counts by category and label, total assessed recommendations, abstentions, and coverage; check agreement through independent annotation or direct panel feedback where available. No panel results were supplied, so counts cannot yet be reported. Abstain specifically on unsupported judgments; [selective-prediction research (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.15610) motivates evaluating accuracy alongside coverage, although its evidence comes from vision-language tasks, not recommendation.

Training implications remain hypotheses: confirmed compatibility conflicts or feedback-confirmed irrelevant near-neighbors could motivate hard-negative sampling; repeated timestamp-supported context mismatches could motivate recency weighting. [Adaptive Hardness Negative Sampling (2024)](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/28709) motivates controlling negative difficulty, while [Enhanced Bayesian Personalized Ranking (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.19276) warns that hard negatives can actually be positives. Keep ambiguous complements, possible redundancy, and abstentions out of explicit-negative labels. Compare changes using the pinned four-category macro validation HR@10; panel judgments diagnose errors but do not replace benchmark selection.
